A coin is flipped $8$ times. Let $X$ represent the number of times the coin lands on heads. Under the null hypothesis that the coin is fair, what are the critical values of a two-tailed test at a significance level of $10%$?

*Hint: You may use the table below, representing the probability distribution of $X$ under the null hypothesis.*

| $x$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ | $5$ | $6$ | $7$ | $8$ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| $P(X = x)$ | $0.0039$ | $0.0313$ | $0.1094$ | $0.2188$ | $0.2734$ | $0.2188$ | $0.1094$ | $0.0313$ | $0.0039$ |

> A calculator is required to answer this question.

A gym has recently moved location, and the owner thinks this could impact the number of customers. The average number of visitors per hour at the old site was $2.5$. Let $X$ represent the number of customers visiting the gym in the new location during a one-hour period. Under the null hypothesis that the number of customers is the same as before, what are the critical values of a two-tailed test at a significance level of $10%$?

*Hint: You may use the table below, representing the cumulative distribution function of $X$ under the null hypothesis.*

| $x$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ | $5$ | $6$ | $⋯$ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| $P(X \le x)$ | $0.0821$ | $0.2873$ | $0.5438$ | $0.7576$ | $0.8912$ | $0.9580$ | $0.9858$ | $⋯$ |

> A calculator is required to answer this question.
